lesson_title: Reteach and varied practice: selection and sequencing
essential_question: How can understanding curating, portfolio, and exhibition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for selection and sequencing, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of selection and sequencing.
Check, revise, or improve work about selection and sequencing using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about selection and sequencing.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 8 of "Curating, Portfolio, and Exhibition" (unit 6, grade 7) is a varied re-practice on selection and sequencing. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Curate a cross-arts portfolio or exhibition with contextual labels and process evidence. Today's work contributes to that by handling selection and sequencing at the reteach and varied practice stage, against the unit's wider topics of curatorial theme, selection and sequencing, artist statements, and audience experience. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Return to selection and sequencing using a different medium or approach than your last attempt — if you worked visually, try it structurally or in writing; if you worked by ear, try it on paper. Make three short varied studies, spaced rather than all at once, and write after each what this approach made clear that the previous one did not. This work is not graded for quality; it is checked for whether your understanding of selection and sequencing now holds up in more than one form. Keep it private. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about selection and sequencing, and it belongs to "Curating, Portfolio, and Exhibition", which also covers separate topics such as curatorial theme. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about selection and sequencing; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting selection and sequencing.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for selection and sequencing follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for selection and sequencing, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for selection and sequencing works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of selection and sequencing, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking selection and sequencing mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply selection and sequencing under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on selection and sequencing rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
